Qualified clock dependency — accepted user decision, 2026-10-10

Authority: the user selected "Allow the qualified clock dependency (recommended)"
in response to the clock question on 2026-10-10. The separately accepted
all-owner-loss decision is recorded below.

The first profile may condition its physical UTC deadline on a named, qualified
clock dependency remaining within a stated error bound. It must test its response
to reported faults. It need not promise detection of every silent clock error.
If that dependency silently exceeds its bound, the physical deadline can be
missed; detection must retain the failure evidence, not report the bound as met.

This decision approves no numeric skew, horizon or enforcement allowance. It does
not qualify a source or establish the missing Fargate evidence semantics. T-01
must still establish a coherent current UTC interval, source/sample relationship,
freshness, timescale, validity/holdover and conservative local deadline binding.
Reported faults and uncertainty require the selected fail-closed response; unknown
required properties reject before sensitive input release.

Keep the original absolute expiry fixed. Restart, resume or new time evidence must
not renew work authority. Keep uncertain execution, scratch and capacity fenced.
Admit no new execution before independently verified termination and required
cleanup. All other isolation, resource, result, recovery, clock/reboot and hosted
evidence requirements remain. T-01 remains incomplete.

All-owner-loss limit — separately accepted user decision, 2026-10-10

Authority: the user selected "Allow this all-owner-loss limit (recommended)" on
2026-10-10. The question asked whether T-01 may exclude simultaneous loss of every
trusted cleanup owner from the physical deletion deadline, while preserving a
surviving owner for required controller, broker and single-runner failures.

The first profile may exclude simultaneous loss of every trusted cleanup owner
from its physical deletion deadline. Required controller, broker and single-runner
failures still require a surviving owner and proof of the selected bounded cleanup
path. If all owners die, deletion may be late. Record a missed physical bound;
quarantine is not deletion. Keep the original expiry fixed and admit no new
execution before independently verified termination and required cleanup.

This exclusion does not excuse payload-induced loss of all owners through
inadequate isolation or resource protection; that remains a design failure.
The exact owners, authority, resource protection, disposal path and fault evidence
remain to be established. No cleanup mechanism or numeric allowance is adopted.

Both decisions are accepted; neither remains pending. They grant no new implementation, deployment or merge authority. All other requirements and existing holds remain.

Canonical plan: bead show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-01. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Select the first protected profile and simplest feasible execution approach, with reproducible containment/recovery evidence and two materially different deployment models under D-07.

## Context
Resolve D-02/D-04/D-07 before production APIs depend on runtime assumptions. Existing Runledger subprocess ownership does not supply these guarantees.

## Changes
First specify one profile assuming a fully compromised registered workload: protected assets, allowed input/result/filesystem/egress, resource/time limits, plaintext/scratch/result handling and supported enforcement-failure domains. Use one representative registered native workload plus a hostile fixture; keep names/scenarios generic. Inspect versions/licenses, input immutability, native dependencies, subprocesses and scratch requirements. Compare the three D-07 topology families on paper; prove at most two shortlisted mechanisms, not an open-ended runtime survey.
Deliver a deployment/privilege/credential map, explicit operational-cost comparison, observed capability matrix, time/skew/enforcement contract, physical execution identity and backend retry/replacement rules, candidate-result ownership/retention-or-recompute decision, and recovery inventory owner. Separate application portability from executor and operator prerequisites. Identify Linux/macOS controller support and unsupported local profiles; name the actual restricted-hosting target and its required acceptance test without introducing a mandatory cloud dependency.
Rehearse ambiguous execution at full reserved capacity in the bounded spike inventory: who contains/reconciles which infrastructure identity, what permits reuse, what remains quarantined, and what reserved control resources keep recovery possible. Select and record the two deployment models in D-07 and revise T-05/T-06 titles/surfaces and any binding-reuse dependency before downstream work. Keep experiment code separate until adopted; no production abstraction is approved by an unexecuted design. Full native ledger integration belongs to T-03/T-04; this spike must not implement a parallel production queue.

## Recovery
Use disposable synthetic inputs and bounded disposable resources. Stop/fence discovered invocations and retain unresolved evidence; do not broaden host privileges or weaken the profile to make the spike pass. An unsupported requirement becomes a concrete design decision before dependent tasks begin.

## Verification policy
Follow the epic verification and rollout contract and the applicable repository/package guides. Record actual commands, revisions, platform/backend prerequisites and outcomes here. Runtime/security/platform claims require executable evidence; delivery acceptance remains incomplete; dated external evidence below records any partial prework. New public APIs require rustdoc, examples and the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment.

## Reconciled evidence and remaining work — 2026-10-09

Reuse the epic's dated external evidence: 100 paired real-tool fixture matches, 12 synthetic scanner assertions and eight boundary/failure controls, repeated in the packaged image. Dependency inventory, per-job private-root compatibility, content-vs-metadata probes, descriptor closure/leak negative control, selected inherited restrictions, observed resource use and finite local cleanup are executed prework. They do not complete this task. Do not rerun that corpus simply to rediscover it; rerun when changed inputs/mechanisms or unresolved failures warrant it.

Continue from these concrete gaps, preserving every existing acceptance requirement:
1. Define the complete first protected profile and failure assumptions. Decide whether the exercised OS-primitive composition qualifies as a supported established-mechanism binding under D-07/T-05, or choose an existing implementation; do not silently approve a new sandbox.
2. Map trusted bootstrap placement separately from zero-capability children. The diagnostic parent was root with CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, KILL, SETGID, SETUID, SETPCAP, SYS_CHROOT and MKNOD. It did not use Docker --privileged, but does not establish D-07's restriction on privileged orchestration in the application container. A dedicated broker in an existing task is a candidate requiring shared IAM/network, credential/update authority and fault-domain analysis.
3. Prove independent expiry after controller and broker loss separately while the processor environment remains alive. Name the surviving enforcer, absolute expiry, allowed delay and restart/clock behavior. A living driver timer, CPU limit or killing their shared container is insufficient.
4. Establish hard aggregate scratch/result/process bounds and recovery resources under saturation. Local Docker PID controls, per-file FSIZE and sampled peaks are not a verified restricted-hosting mapping or aggregate quota. Rehearse the existing full-capacity ambiguity/reconciliation scenario.
5. Execute the selected restricted-hosting probe only under separate authorization. Fargate remains a candidate target rather than a required provider. Exact capability/device/syscall/PID behavior is unverified. Fresh official scanner signatures, freshness/rotation and full-memory behavior remain consumer prerequisites; synthetic no-match is not a production Clean verdict.
6. Decide physical identity/replacement semantics, last-copy result ownership/retention-or-recompute policy, and two materially different deployments within the existing three-family comparison. Local packaged vs bind-mounted execution is the same deployment model. Update D-07 and T-05/T-06 concrete surfaces and any binding-reuse edge only after those decisions.

Retain all prior negative evidence, including inherited-descriptor leakage and failed harness attempts. The motivating consumer's cancellation/admission ordering defect is unresolved; its causal scenario must not be treated as repaired by the diagnostic's serial reaping. Record real deployment prerequisites and operating cost rather than inferring savings from tiny-database samples. Required unsupported bounds keep the candidate/task incomplete.


## Executed feasibility checkpoint — 2026-10-10

User authorized T-01 continuation after the isolated Fargate compatibility experiment. Production implementation has not started; original acceptance/design/blocker edges remain unchanged.

Actual Fargate platform1.4.0 LinuxX86_64 kernel6.1.186 completed all120 prior real-tool/synthetic assertions and runtime controls (durable handoff /srv/dev/home/dev/.local/state/dealsafe-overseer/pr98-fargate-standalone-20261010). This supersedes only the earlier unknown restricted-runtime compatibility, not full D02/D04/D07 acceptance.

New bounded local causal test: nofault and controller-killed cases stopped at2.013s and2.018s for a2s deadline; broker-killed processor and descendant stayed alive through3.504s until owned cleanup, with independent environment heartbeats. The current broker timer fails independent expiry. Resource negativecontrols demonstrated aggregate growth beyond individual FSIZE/AS limits and open-unlinked bytes omitted by directory accounting.

New isolated AWS prerequisite run, task7cf2fbce92404cdf90e8a3ca2e95e54c, image sha256:fe3b56903822af05dcb90477ca93763b180e7ce53364ad12df80810e2f5ae134: user namespace attempts and tmpfs mount returnedEPERM; memory/PID cgroup child creation returnedEROFS. All12 visible cgroup mounts were readonly. The probe's own network/io_uring-only filter allows namespace/mount syscalls; denial source inside the provider is not attributed. Existing /dev/shm was4092735488bytes/999203inodes/noexec, not localDocker64MiB; no per-job quota/exhaustion or protected recovery headroom was proved. These observations reject the tested in-task Bubblewrap prerequisites, not all possible Fargate designs.

All24 runtime events, source/image identity and STOPPED gates validated. TaskSTOPPED09:17:46UTC; cleanup APIs09:18:08; independent readback09:20:18 confirmed own VPC/subnet/route/IGW/SG/ECR/role/loggroup absent and clusterINACTIVE. Taskdefinition metadata remainedDELETE_IN_PROGRESS; no running resources or shared staging/Terraform mutation. Local failed harness/schema evidence and11 invalid-result controls are retained.

Durable continuation bundle: /srv/dev/home/dev/.local/state/dealsafe-overseer/batter-t01-feasibility-20261010/REPORT.txt. It includes exact source/build/receipts, lifetime/resource reports, independent diagnostic inspection, three-family topology/privilege/cost comparison and a concrete PROFILE-PROPOSAL fixed before further full mechanism selection/proof. The profile is proposed/unverified, not an adopted production guarantee.

Disposition: T-01 remains open/incomplete. The exercised primitive composition lacks independent broker-loss expiry and verified aggregate scratch/resource enforcement; it is not approved as a new sandbox. No two supported models have been selected. Remaining clock/restart/replacement/result-loss/full-capacity recovery acceptance is unexecuted. T-02 stays blocked; T-05/T-06 scopes/dependencies stay unchanged. Next material decision is whether an established executor outside the restricted application task is acceptable, or same-task Fargate remains mandatory. Neither separate native-worker placement nor disposable per-job Fargate automatically supplies the missing guarantees. Do not relax strict no-overlap, per-job filesystem/resource boundaries or independent expiry to proceed. The motivating PR98's merge hold, separate cancellation/admission P1 and hosted acceptance remain unresolved.

## Accepted first-profile host assumption — 2026-10-10

First-profile host assumption — accepted user decision, 2026-10-10.
Authority: the user selected "Allow the functioning-host assumption (recommended)" in the supervisor conversation on 2026-10-10 and explicitly relayed that decision in the owning agent thread on the same date. This answers and supersedes the earlier pending host-failure question; it does not supersede the recorded failure evidence.
The first profile may require a functioning, unpaused kernel, scheduler and I/O for its physical cleanup deadline. A full host freeze can delay physical cleanup. Record that delay as a missed physical bound for that fault; do not report quarantine as physical deletion or claim the hard cleanup bound was met.
Keep the original absolute expiry fixed. Never renew it on restart or resume. Uncertain execution, scratch and capacity remain fenced. Admit no new execution before independently verified termination and required cleanup. This decision does not grant expired work new authority or resolve whether a payload can run before its owner after resume.
Post-resume execution-authority/scheduling behavior, owner-death recovery, trusted time-source/clock/reboot fault coverage and hosted proof retain their existing evidence requirements. Numeric profile limits remain proposed and unapproved. T-01 stays incomplete. All other isolation, resource, recovery, result and strict no-overlap guarantees remain unchanged. This decision grants no new deployment, source-edit or review-controller authority and does not lift the motivating consumer's explicit merge hold.

Continue the existing authorized design work using this decision. Do not wait for or route routine coordination to the supervisor again on this point. The provider-independent Batter contract and the consuming application's existing-task placement remain fixed; no additional temporary or permanent product task is selected.
